headline.title: The same budget now does {factor} times the work.
headline.analogy: Think of a car that suddenly goes many times further on the same tank. Same tank, same road, same driver, and the same tests checking the work.
headline.caption: Cost per worker job, 25 matched jobs, API-equivalent pricing.

intro: Every figure on this page comes from a dated record of our own machine and our own AI workers. Each one is labelled MEASURED or MODELLED, and each one says how it was taken. Figures still being taken show as measuring, and are filled in when the record exists.

metrics.label: Memory in use on the build machine
metrics.method: Windows memory reading while the fleet ran idle-looking; 28 of 31 GB in use before the work. Round 2 re-reads the same counter.

metrics.label: CPU busy while 'doing nothing'
metrics.method: Windows CPU reading before the work. Round 2 re-reads it with the fleet running under its new ceilings.

metrics.label: Windows VM memory (vmmem) after a cache trim
metrics.method: Measured around one cache-trim run: 13.0 GB before, 7.4 GB 20 seconds later. A scheduled trim now runs every 10 minutes.

metrics.label: Load the worker fleet was allowed to put on 8 cores
metrics.method: Configured ceiling, read from the fleet governor settings: allowed load 24 before, 6 after. Workers dropped from 12 to 3 per account.
metrics.note: A ceiling, not an observed load. Observed load is a round-2 figure.

metrics.label: Observed load average (24 hour mean)
metrics.method: Round 2: mean load average over 24 hours before and after, from the machine's own counters.

metrics.label: Memory per headless worker spent on tool servers
metrics.method: Each worker started about 7 tool servers (about 550 MB); a strict config now starts none.

metrics.label: Cron work per 24 hour day
metrics.method: Summed run time of every scheduled job over 3 days of run records, per day. Round 2 repeats the sum on the same record.
metrics.note: Job-hours can exceed 24 because jobs overlap.

metrics.label: Failure rate of the 5-minute state snapshot job
metrics.method: 256 of 287 runs failed (89.2%), so state was not reaching the remote copy. The fix is in; the after rate needs a fresh run record.

metrics.label: 5-minute snapshot, time per run
metrics.method: Run record average before, a timed run after. The secret check now scans only files that could be committed.

metrics.label: Cloud mirror, time per run
metrics.method: Before: 30 to 45 minutes a run (midpoint shown, 37.5 minutes). After: 14 seconds, incremental with a daily full pass.
metrics.note: Before is the midpoint of a 30 to 45 minute range.

metrics.label: Progress ping, time per run
metrics.method: Ping re-ran a test suite that always timed out. The result is now cached until the code changes.

metrics.label: Repository bundle step, time per run
metrics.method: One bundle per repository keyed on content, instead of re-bundling about 12 worktrees.

metrics.label: Most jobs firing in one minute
metrics.method: Counted from the schedule. A lint check now fails any minute with more than 5 jobs.

metrics.label: Backup success rate
metrics.method: Round 2: successful runs over total runs for the backup jobs, before and after, from run records.

metrics.label: Files the cloud sync client tracks
metrics.method: File count before; about 142,700 after a duplicate rolling copy (92,538 files) was excluded and moved out.

metrics.label: Fleet throughput (jobs completed per day)
metrics.method: Round 2: completed worker jobs per day from the fleet ledger, before and after the ceilings.

metrics.label: Jobs per hour
metrics.method: Round 2: completed jobs divided by active hours, from the fleet ledger.

metrics.label: Tokens a worker reads before its first action
metrics.method: Counted at session start across 198 worker sessions (before, about 215k, because the rule book loaded twice) against sessions on the compact core (about 29k).

metrics.label: Cost per worker job (API-equivalent)
metrics.method: 25 matched jobs: same task text as earlier runs on the full rule book, re-run on the compact core. Cost is API-equivalent token pricing, not a bill.
metrics.source: Kernel compression gate record, 2026-10-08; Sigil ceiling report, 2026-10-08

metrics.label: Daily spend, modelled ceiling
metrics.method: The same measured token counts repriced under five layers of change. The last layer needs a decision not yet taken. A scenario, not a forecast.

metrics.label: Recall test, 50 questions
metrics.method: 50 questions about the rule book, read-only tools, judged. Before is the full rule book, after is the compact core. Bar was 48 or better.

metrics.label: Held-out recall test, 25 questions
metrics.method: Questions written by an independent agent that never saw the compact core.

metrics.label: Fully good results on 25 matched jobs
metrics.method: Same 25 tasks. Two full-rule-book results claimed clean lint on files that fail lint. The compact core had none.

metrics.label: Kernel compression gate
metrics.method: The compact core is 17,143 bytes. It must clear the bar before it is allowed to load.

metrics.label: Interactive session start
metrics.method: Tokens before the first reply with the old and new kernel layout.

metrics.label: Session start inside the main codebase
metrics.method: Tokens before the first reply after 18 reference files moved to on-demand loading. The full test suite stayed green.

metrics.label: Main codebase test suite run time
metrics.method: Wall-clock seconds for the full suite, before and after.

metrics.label: Kernel gate run time
metrics.method: Round 2: wall-clock seconds for the kernel verify gate, before and after.

metrics.label: Editor hook time per edit
metrics.method: Seconds of hook time per file edit, before and after.

metrics.label: Reply hook time per reply
metrics.method: Seconds removed from every reply. Saved time is the figure supplied; before and after are filed with the log.

metrics.label: Kernel repository size
metrics.method: Size of the repository directory before and after history and run-state cleanup.

metrics.label: Disk freed from stale worktrees
metrics.method: Gigabytes freed by removing finished worktrees.

timeline.text: 198 worker sessions found loading the rule book twice, about 215k tokens before the first action. It stopped on its own; a guard and an hourly audit now watch for it.
Schedule paused and backed up while the heaviest jobs were measured and rewritten.
Compact kernel core cleared its recall gate, 48 of 50 plus 24 of 25 on questions it had never seen.
25-job matched kill test finished: 25 of 25 fully good against 23 of 25, at US$0.116 against US$0.973 per job.
Interactive and main-codebase session starts measured on the new layout.

hardening.label: Tests passing in the main codebase
hardening.method: Overridden at render from the ledger.

hardening.label: Adversary reviews
hardening.method: Count of independent reviews that tried to break a change before it merged.

hardening.label: Chaos drills
hardening.method: Count of deliberate failure drills against the fleet.

hardening.label: Mutation checks
hardening.method: Count of deliberately broken lines that the tests caught.

hardening.label: Restore drills
hardening.method: Count of times a backup was restored and checked.
